title: Quantum Fourier transform for the symmetric group
authors: Carli Bruinsma, Dmitry Grinko, Maris Ozols
abstract: Quantum Fourier transforms (QFT) for general groups were recognized to be fundamental already early in the field. A canonical example of non-abelian QFT for the symmetric group was outlined by Beals (1997). Later, a more detailed analysis of this algorithm was carried out by Kawano and Sekigawa (2016). In this paper, we revisit that construction. After a careful analysis, we revise their gate complexity to $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(n^{3.5})$ and circuit depth to $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(n^3)$. Moreover, we observe that their construction is not optimal in the choice of transversal elements, so we propose simpler realization of the symmetric group QFT.
summary: This paper provides a detailed, gate-level analysis and improved construction for the Quantum Fourier Transform specific to the symmetric group $S_n$. By analyzing the structure through Young tableaux and subgroup chains, the authors refine the gate complexity bounds, offering a more rigorous quantum circuit blueprint for this fundamental operation.
main_problem: The paper aims to develop an efficient, low-level quantum circuit implementation for the Quantum Fourier Transform (QFT) associated with the symmetric group ($S_n$).
main_result: The authors revise previous complexity bounds, proposing a simplified realization of the $S_n$ QFT with improved gate complexity compared to prior literature.
method: The approach involves decomposing the unitary operator into elementary one- and two-qubit gates by leveraging the structure of $S_n$ representations via subgroup chains and Young tableaux.
model_or_system: The system is the symmetric group $S_n$, whose representations are indexed by integer partitions ($\lambda \vdash n$). The computation is realized through unitary transformations derived from restriction and induction operations along the subgroup chain $S_1 \subset S_2 \subset \cdots \subset S_n$.
key_observables: Gate complexity (depth and number of gates), circuit depth, and the structure of the unitary operator $U(m)_{Ind}$.
important_parameters: The size parameter $n$ (or $m$), and the integer partition $\lambda$ defining the representation.
main_assumptions: The derivation assumes that the required unitary operators can be decomposed into basic one- and two-qubit gates and coherent arithmetic operations, and relies on the correctness of inductive steps.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the Bratteli diagram for $S_5$, the circuit structure for the inductive step $U(m)_{Ind}$, and diagrams detailing how local structural changes (addable/removable cells) affect the determinant signs.
paper_structure: The paper reviews prior QFT constructions, establishes the mathematical framework using Young tableaux and subgroup chains, derives the circuit for the inductive step $U(m)_{Ind}$ by analyzing gate cancellations, and concludes by determining the signs of associated determinants.
why_interesting: The rigorous, low-level circuit decomposition of a group-theoretic quantum transform is highly relevant for developing practical quantum algorithms for representation theory, which underpins many quantum simulation tasks.
